record.original_question: Can one characterize the groups pi_1^(r)(X) geometrically, without referring to stratified vector bundles; equivalently, can one describe which Galois coverings of X have the property that the natural surjection pi_1(X) -> G factors through pi_1^(r)(X)?

evidence.quote: Question 4.5 Can we characterize the pi1^(r)(X)s geometrically: that means without any mention of stratified vector bundles? By this we mean that we can characterize the Galois coverings of X whose group surjection pi1(X) -> G factors through pi1^(r)(X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected variety over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with a chosen geometric base point $x \in X(k)$. For each integer $r \geq 0$, let $\mathrm{Strat}^{(r)}(X)$ denote the full Tannakian subcategory of the category $\mathrm{Strat}(X)$ of stratified vector bundles on $X$ generated by those stratified bundles whose underlying $\mathcal{O}_X$-coherent module has rank $\leq r$ (with the natural notion of subobjects, quotients, tensor products, and duals inherited from $\mathrm{Strat}(X)$). The fiber functor at $x$ makes $\mathrm{Strat}^{(r)}(X)$ neutral Tannakian over $k$, and one defines the affine $k$-group scheme
$$\pi_1^{(r)}(X,x) := \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}\bigl(\omega_x|_{\mathrm{Strat}^{(r)}(X)}\bigr),$$
together with the natural faithfully flat homomorphism $\pi_1(X,x) \twoheadrightarrow \pi_1^{(r)}(X,x)$ from the (Tannakian) fundamental group of $\mathrm{Strat}(X)$.

Provide a purely geometric characterization of the groups $\pi_1^{(r)}(X,x)$ that does not refer to stratified vector bundles. Equivalently, describe intrinsically (in geometric terms involving $X$ and its coverings) which finite Galois étale coverings $Y \to X$ with Galois group $G$ have the property that the canonical surjection $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,x) \twoheadrightarrow G$ factors through the maximal pro-étale quotient of $\pi_1^{(r)}(X,x)$.
artifact.category_tag: stratified fundamental group in positive characteristic
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for a geometric (covering-theoretic) description of the rank-bounded stratified fundamental group quotients $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$. Subsequent work of Esnault–Mehta and others on stratified bundles and the étale fundamental group in characteristic $p$ has clarified relationships between stratified bundles and $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}$, but no explicit geometric characterization of all $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$ (for general $r$) without reference to stratified bundles appears to have been established in the literature available.

status_evidence.title: Stratified bundles and étale fundamental group
status_evidence.snippet: Esnault–Mehta study stratified bundles and prove e.g. that on simply connected projective manifolds in char p there are no nontrivial stratified bundles, but do not give a covering-theoretic description of all π_1^{(r)}.
status_evidence.claim: Related results connect stratified bundles to π_1^{ét} but do not provide a full geometric characterization of π_1^{(r)}.

status_evidence.title: The étale fundamental group and F-divided sheaves in characteristic p>0
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate the relation between F-divided/stratified sheaves and the étale fundamental group, indicating the question remains an active research direction.
status_evidence.claim: The geometric meaning of rank-bounded stratified fundamental groups is still being explored.
